source: Bram Stoker, Dracula, 1897 (public domain). Summarised in our own words.
canon_beats: Jonathan arrives at Castle Dracula and is received by the Count.
Jonathan realises he is a prisoner; escapes.
Lucy sickens in Whitby; Van Helsing is called in.
Lucy dies and returns; the men destroy the vampire she has become.
Dracula turns his attention to Mina; she is bitten and bound to him.
The hunters pursue Dracula back to Transylvania and destroy him at sunset.

entry.opening_npc_line: Madam Mina, it is Van Helsing. Will you let me in? I bring garlic and a crucifix for your protection.
entry.opening_clip_prompt: First-person POV of a young woman sitting up in a canopied bed in a Victorian bedroom, 1897: dark oak panelling, a single candle guttering on the nightstand, moonlight through lace curtains, a heavy locked door. Three firm knocks shake the door. Slow push-in toward the door. An older man's voice, muffled through the wood, S1: "Madam Mina, it is Van Helsing. Will you let me in? I bring garlic and a crucifix for your protection." Candle flame crackles, wind rattles the window, floorboards creak beyond the door.

jonathan.opening_npc_line: Friend Jonathan, the Count is in London. Tell me everything you saw in his castle. Spare nothing.
jonathan.opening_clip_prompt: First-person POV of a man seated in a gaslit study at a Victorian asylum, 1897: green-shaded lamp, a travel journal open on the desk, barred window black with night. Across the desk an older white-haired man leans forward, eyes sharp with urgency. Slow push-in on his face. He speaks, S1: "Friend Jonathan, the Count is in London. Tell me everything you saw in his castle. Spare nothing." A clock ticks, the gas flame hisses, a patient cries far down the corridor.

locations.harker_room: The Harkers' bedroom at Dr Seward's asylum: canopied bed, oak panelling, candlelight, a heavy door, a casement window over the grounds.
locations.castle_hall: The great hall of Castle Dracula: cold stone, iron-bound doors, torchlight, dust of centuries.
locations.whitby_cliff: The cliff at Whitby: ruined abbey above, grey sea below, gravestones leaning in the wind.
locations.asylum: Dr Seward's asylum: gaslit corridors, barred windows, distant cries of patients.
locations.graveyard: A London churchyard at night: yew trees, leaning headstones, the Westenra tomb.

forks.title: Refuse the door
forks.trigger_hint: Mina tells Van Helsing no and keeps the door shut
forks.dawn_description: She is pale, the window open, two marks on her neck; Van Helsing outside, grim.
forks.dawn_clip_prompt: First-person POV waking in a Victorian bedroom at cold grey dawn, 1897. The casement window hangs open, lace curtains soaked and stirring; the candle is burned out. Looking down: a woman's pale trembling hands. In a silver hand-mirror on the quilt, two small red puncture marks on a pale neck. Slow tilt up to the doorway where an older white-haired man stands grim and silent, hat in hand. A distant church bell tolls, raw wind gusts through the open window, one long floorboard creak.

forks.title: Invite the Count in
forks.trigger_hint: Mina invites Dracula (the Count) in, not Van Helsing
forks.dawn_description: The room is empty, the bed unslept in, a bat's shadow on the wall; Jonathan waking alone.
forks.dawn_clip_prompt: First-person POV of a man stepping into an empty Victorian bedroom at dawn, 1897. The bed is made and unslept in, a crucifix lies face-down on the floorboards, the window open to a bruised orange sky. On the whitewashed wall the shadow of a great bat slides across and vanishes. Handheld step forward toward the empty bed. A man's voice cracks, S1: "Mina? MINA!" Then only wind through the window, and far off, a single wolf howl.

forks.title: Tell the truth early
forks.trigger_hint: Mina tells Van Helsing about her dreams before he asks
forks.dawn_description: She wakes safe, the room fortified, Van Helsing asleep in a chair.
forks.dawn_clip_prompt: First-person POV waking safe in a Victorian bedroom at golden dawn, 1897. Ropes of garlic flowers ring the closed casement window, a small crucifix is nailed above the headboard, wax seals dot the door frame. In an armchair beside the bed an older white-haired man sleeps upright, a leather book open on his chest. Gentle pan from the bright window to the chair. Birdsong outside, coals settling in the grate, his slow steady snoring.
